# the contributor audit of all-status anchored residual credit and its exact scalar limit

Source: `candidate 6d98cff7cbcfe25c`, all sections. Verdict: PASS. The deterministic point, all ambient normals, residual status distinctions, and constants are checked below.

When captured source mass B is at least the smallest source volume, the proposed credit is bounded by that volume and no Brunn--Minkowski assertion is needed. If B is smaller, every source residual has positive volume. Positive barycentric averaging preserves the strict complementary halfspace inequality and gives an actual subset of the anchor residual. Closure is harmless for nonzero continuous normals because their boundaries have zero d-volume. For zero continuous normal, the nonempty residual fibers are whole fibers and the strict base inequalities also put the whole anchor fiber in the residual. Thus the root-sum inequality is valid in both cases.

The depletion functions are increasing and convex and vanish at zero. Restricting them to [0,B] gives f_j(U_j)<=(U_j/B)f_j(B). Summation and inversion give the stated credit. The zero-budget and zero-defect cases are separately covered. A truncated minimizing inverse at the full source volume never enters the positive-residual argument. The scalar exactness claim is correctly limited to these alternatives, rather than geometric realizability.

At one actual point in the anchor fiber, the own capture is at least its known ordinary depth and the residual budget is at most the complementary own volume. Monotonicity of the credit has the correct direction. The fractional packing counts each other source volume at most once and has a compact feasible polytope. It constructs no averaged or randomized point.

For the thirteen-volume application, the three displayed bases average exactly to the chosen anchor. Assuming total capture at most 1/100 leaves each residual positive. Weighted Brunn--Minkowski followed by ordinary three-term AM-GM gives the displayed product bound in every d. The rational product gap is positive; the elementary exponential-series bound gives Gamma_d>4/11, while binomial expansion gives Gamma_d<=1/2. Therefore the actual anchor centroid has uniform raw depth at least Gamma_d/7+3/1300. The strict pointwise three-fiber inequality is not used to assert an unjustified strict infimum; the fixed positive surplus does that work.

## Exact obstruction to a volume-only completion

The new theorem is valid, but its centroid-plus-credit certificate alone cannot imply OC for all compatible volume data, even with all anchored relations and optimal fractional packing.

Take three consecutive bases -1,0,1 in integer dimension one, continuous dimension d=2, and homothetic common-vertex triangular fibers with respective areas

    (a,k,b)=(1/4,1,1).

For example choose any area-one triangle T with a vertex at zero and set the fibers to (1/2)T,T,T. Their endpoint midpoint is (3/4)T subset T, so these are exact fibers of an actual convex body. The middle centroid's exact own ordinary raw depth is Gamma_2 k=4/9. There is only one nontrivial extreme anchored relation: the middle base is the midpoint of the endpoints. No endpoint has a representation by other bases.

For the middle residual budget h=5/9, the pair credit is

    R=a-(2 sqrt(h)-sqrt(b))^2
      =4 sqrt(5)/3-107/36>0.

The smaller-volume source gives the minimum inverse: its depletion derivative is at least that of the larger source throughout [0,a], so the convex concentration proof allocates to it first. Alternatively direct substitution in the two displayed inverse formulas gives the same minimum. Positivity follows from 48^2*5>107^2, and the credit is below a.

The three candidate certificate values are therefore

    1/9, 4 sqrt(5)/3-91/36, 4/9.

Their maximum is the middle value, and it is strictly smaller than

    (Gamma_2/2)(a+k+b)=1/2,

because 48 sqrt(5)<109, certified by 48^2*5<109^2. With one relation the fractional-packing weight is at most one, so packing cannot raise this certificate. Nonextreme repetitions of the same anchored relation contain no new scalar information.

This is an exact failure of the proposed universal scalar certificate, not of OC, not of the residual theorem, and not of actual centroid depths. The actual caps couple directions across the shapes; replacing them by independent own-depth and residual-volume bounds discards that information. A continuation through this interface must retain such geometric coupling or choose additional actual points.
